messages:
Mari: heads-up — nightly-gpu is red on a100-80gb pool. Failing test: transformer_inference_test::test_long_sequence_batch. CI job: https://ci.internal/runs/98765 :sob:

sre-bot: CI job 98765 failed on runner gpu-a100-07, status: FAILED, exit 137. Rerun: /rerun 98765

Ash: ok looking. can you paste the last 200 lines of the job log and dmesg?

Mari: pasted minimal logs below — truncated, but shows the OOM/hang and a dmesg GPU hang (Xid 79):

```
2026-03-17T03:12:05Z INFO Running tests: transformer_inference_test::test_long_sequence_batch
2026-03-17T03:12:25Z ERROR cuda: alloc failed for 35389440 bytes: out of memory
2026-03-17T03:12:25Z ERROR RuntimeError: failed to allocate KV cache for seq_len=4096
... stack trace ...
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, Channel: 00000001, engine: 13, Arg1: 00000000, Arg2: 00000000, Ref: 0x1a2b3c
[ 1234.568900] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0 has fallen off the bus.
```

Mari: the test sometimes passes locally on a smaller sequence; flaky on CI only. No recent code in the test itself. We did bump the nightly base image last night: `nlp-runtime:cuda-12.1.2-2026-03-16`

Luke: ping @Ash — any agent/driver flips on that image bump? Could be userland/kernel mismatch. :eyes:

Ash: The image bump pulled in `libnvidia-allocator 1.2.0` and an updated nvidia driver package `535.104`. We didn't change kernel modules on the host. That mismatch can cause weird allocation failures.

Sam: can we try a focused rerun on the same runner with the previous image? Dev CI supports rerun-with-image.

dev-ci: Command to rerun with previous image:
```
ci rerun 98765 --image nlp-runtime:cuda-12.1.0-stable --runner gpu-a100-07
```

Mari: triggered rerun with previous image, job 98766. Also started a single-test run to reduce noise:
```
python -m pytest tests/transformer_inference_test.py::test_long_sequence_batch -k "gpu" -q
```

dev-ci: Rerun 98766 queued on gpu-a100-07.

Ash: quick check — can you also capture `nvidia-smi -q` and `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` from the failing run?

Mari: pasted snippets:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q | head -n 10
Driver Version                          : 535.104.01
CUDA Version                            : 12.1
fb_memory_usage
    Total                               : 81920 MiB
    Used                                : 79310 MiB
    Free                                : 2610 MiB
```

```
$ cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module  535.104.01  Wed Jan 31 2026
GCC version: 9.3.0
```

Luke: free memory looks low on that node (Used ~79GB). Could be a leak from previous job not cleaned up. Are we sure runner cleans driver allocations between jobs?

Ash: we run `nvidia-smi -r` in between jobs; that should reset. But pinned host allocations (from libnvidia-allocator) sometimes survive if process didn't exit cleanly.

Sam: 98766 finished — green on previous image. That points to something introduced by the new image.

Mari: confirmed: 98766 passed on `nlp-runtime:cuda-12.1.0-stable`. 98765 failed on `cuda-12.1.2` image.

Ash: ok this narrows it. Likely transient allocation behavior from `libnvidia-allocator 1.2.0`. Can we bisect the image layers? Which package bumped?

Mari: image diff between tags: bumped `libnvidia-allocator` 1.1.8 -> 1.2.0, `nccl` 2.18.5 -> 2.18.6, and glibc minor patch.

Luke: first priority — prevent flaky CI by pinning to stable image for nightly until we investigate. @dev-ci can we set nightly-gpu to use `cuda-12.1.0-stable` until EOW?

dev-ci: Done — nightly-gpu pinned to nlp-runtime:cuda-12.1.0-stable.

Ash: next steps: reproduce locally with the newer allocator lib. Mari — can you run a small stress loop on a100 with long sequences and monitor `pmap` / `nvidia-smi` to see if allocations accumulate across processes? Example command:
```
for i in {1..30}; do python -c "import inference; inference.run_stress(seq_len=4096, batch=2)"; sleep 2; nvidia-smi; done
```

Mari: running that now on gpu-a100-03. I see allocations creeping up and not freeing between iterations. Attaching a short trace — looks like libcudart calls to `cudaHostAlloc` are higher than expected.

Sam: sounds like pinned memory leak in userland. Could be allocator wrapper changed behavior to use persistent host allocations for caching. That interacts badly with our test harness which expects process-level cleanup.

Ash: action: open a bisect ticket against image layers and patch libnvidia-allocator to 1.1.8 in preprod image to validate. If validated, we rollback image in prod images and file an upstream bug with allocator. I'll take that.

Mari: ACK — filing ticket now: https://issues.internal/RED-2334 (image:libnvidia-allocator leak on 1.2.0)

Luke: nice triage. For immediate CI stability: keep pinned image, add an extra post-job `nvidia-persistenced --terminate` + `pkill -9 cuda_worker` cleanup step in the runner to be extra safe.

Ash: I'll add the cleanup step and start the image bisect. ETA EOD for patch test.

Sam: thanks all :thumbsup:

Mari: thanks — will monitor nightly and reopen if anything else pops up."
